title: Presence via a signed bridge heartbeat to the api
summary: POST /api/devices/heartbeat (device-signed, replay-guarded, copying the transport-report pattern) and a status derived from last_seen_at at read time; bridge presence.rs posts every 30 s. Relay's status POST still runs this stage so nothing user-visible changes.

title: Shrink the relay to rendezvous
summary: Delete device_key/device_online/device_offline fan-out, transport_key, and the status POST from the relay and the bridge relay client; frame cap 64 KiB, queue 1 MiB; serve_device/serve_client under the clippy threshold with both ratchets retired (23→21); relay tests, dev_relay example and k8s yaml updated.

title: The bridge refuses to be relayed, and signaling is carrier-neutral
summary: session_accept returns over the carrier the session_init arrived on (the seam a direct-network listener reuses); non-rtc.* frames on a Relay carrier are refused with relay_is_not_a_data_plane; FellBack becomes ChannelsLost and the admin bucket relay_only becomes never_connected.

title: Prefer direct: mDNS, interface policy, relay acceptance delay
summary: A SettingEngine on the bridge peer: mDNS QueryOnly so browser host candidates resolve on a LAN, UDP4/UDP6 non-loopback gathering, a relay-pair acceptance delay, BRIDGE_ICE_POLICY=direct-only that strips TURN, and BRIDGE_ICE_INTERFACES; parsed fail-fast with tests.

title: SPA core: the rendezvous seam per device, no terminal socket
summary: core/rendezvous.js replaces relayLink.js (both ratchets retired, 61→59): one rendezvous per device context mints its sessions with no device_key wait and no background reconnect; sessionSwitch makes the peer the only active carrier and queues calls until it arrives; peerLink gains onConnected/onFailed; TerminalSocket is handed a minted session and a term carrier and never owns a socket.

title: SPA policy: live only over channels, fail closed per device, presence from the api
summary: Per device: rendezvous → mint → negotiate → close the socket → land; any failure blocks that device with a reason in the existing away vocabulary and a Retry control, the account-wide hold only when none is live; presence and late-device join come from a 15 s GET /api/devices poll; terminals follow a device by minting through its rendezvous; the device-settings socket is retired; browser pass on the two-bridge stack.

title: QA over the peer path, deploy, docs
summary: The Node harnesses gain a WebRTC path (werift or node-datachannel): client.mjs mints over the relay, negotiates the two channels, closes the socket, and every existing qa/e2e/wire-check check runs over the DataChannel, plus a relay-refusal check; README, HANDOFF, deploy docs and the older WebRTC spec updated.
